subtopics.title: What Development Means and How It Is Measured

questions.question: Economic growth and development differ in that:
options: Growth is more output measured in money; development asks whether lives improve in health, education and choice
Growth only happens in developing countries
Development is measured in GDP and growth in HDI
They are identical concepts

questions.question: The Gini coefficient measures:
options: The total size of an economy
Average years of schooling
Inequality of income distribution, from zero at perfect equality toward one
The number of people below a poverty line

questions.question: The Human Development Index combines:
options: Exports, imports and savings
A long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living
Population, area and density
Birth rate, death rate and migration

questions.question: A fair criticism of Rostow's model is that it:
options: Has too few stages to describe any economy
Only applies to African countries
Ignores economics entirely
Assumes every country repeats the West's staircase, ignoring colonial history and late-starter disadvantages

subtopics.title: Trade, Aid and the Rules of the Game

questions.question: The terms of trade move against raw-material exporters because:
options: Primary prices swing and drift downward against the steadier, rising prices of manufactured imports
Shipping costs fall every year
Manufactured goods get cheaper faster than ore
Raw materials cannot be exported legally

questions.question: Beneficiation means:
options: Receiving development aid from a donor
Processing your own raw materials to capture the value added before export
Subsidising imports of machinery
Reducing tariffs on foreign goods

questions.question: Tied or conditional aid is aid that:
options: Is delivered only after a disaster
Passes through the World Bank
Comes with strings, such as spending it on the donor's goods or adopting the donor's policies
Can never be repaid

questions.question: The dependency argument against long-term food aid is that it can:
options: Make recipients too wealthy
Only reach urban areas
Expire before arrival
Undercut local farmers' prices and destroy the local production it should be building

subtopics.title: Powering the Country — Conventional and Non-Conventional Energy

questions.question: The energy chain inside a coal-fired power station runs:
options: Coal burned, water boiled to steam, steam spins the turbine, turbine spins the generator
Coal crushed, coal spins the turbine directly, electricity stored in the tower
Steam burned, coal boiled, generator heats the turbine
Coal dissolved in water, current extracted chemically

questions.question: Acid mine drainage is:
options: Rainwater draining off power station roofs
The chemical used to wash coal before burning
Water turned acidic in old mine workings, leaking toward rivers
A method of cooling turbines with recycled water

questions.question: Pumped-storage schemes like Ingula act as:
options: The country's main source of new electricity
Giant batteries — pumping water uphill in quiet hours to release through turbines at peak demand
Desalination plants for coastal cities
Flood-control dams on major rivers

questions.question: The main technical limitation of solar and wind power is:
options: Their fuel is the most expensive available
They emit more carbon than coal
They can only be built underground
Intermittency — the sun sets and the wind lulls, so they need storage and flexible backup

subtopics.title: Soil, Sustainability and the Greener Economy

questions.question: Soil is treated as non-renewable because:
options: It takes centuries to form a few centimetres of topsoil, which one storm on bare ground can remove
It cannot be moved between farms
Plants use it up permanently as they grow
South African law classifies it as a mineral

questions.question: The erosion sequence on abused land runs:
options: Donga, then rills, then sheet erosion, then splash
Gully first, then sheet erosion spreads from it
Raindrop splash, sheet erosion, rills, then gullies or dongas
Rills form only after dongas collapse

questions.question: Ploughing along the contours controls erosion because:
options: It loosens soil so water sinks faster downhill
It doubles the speed of runoff
Contour lines mark where erosion cannot happen
Each furrow lies across the slope and acts as a small dam holding water back

questions.question: In the greener economy, the syllabus assigns responsibilities to:
options: Government only
Government, businesses and individuals, each with their own list
Power stations only
International donors only

subtopics.title: The Scoreboard and the Rigged Shop

questions.question: Judging a country by total GDP is like judging a school by total marks because:
options: The biggest school always wins regardless of how its learners actually perform
Marks and money are the same thing
Small schools never do well
GDP already includes education scores

questions.question: In the rigged shop, the trap for raw-material sellers is that:
options: The shop refuses their currency
Raw prices wobble and slide while finished-goods prices march up, so the same ore buys less each year
They may not enter the shop at all
Finished goods are banned from export

questions.question: Aid that builds bakeries beats aid that delivers bread means:
options: Emergency food aid is always wrong
Bakeries are cheaper than bread
Aid that builds local capacity beats permanent handouts that create dependency
Donors should only fund food industries

subtopics.title: The Braai Fire and the Two Free Fuels

questions.question: In the braai picture, baseload is:
options: The steady floor of supply a grid needs, like a fire that burns all night
The biggest single power station
The maximum the grid can ever carry
Electricity used only at midday

questions.question: The Northern Cape suits concentrated solar plants because:
options: It has the country's strongest winds
Its clear dry skies deliver among the best sunshine on the planet, and molten salt storage extends output after dark
It is closest to the coalfields
Its rivers provide cooling water

questions.question: Renewable electricity became cheaper than new coal in South Africa largely because:
options: Coal ran out in Mpumalanga
Government banned coal construction
Turbines and panels last forever
Competitive bidding rounds pulled private investors into wind and solar and drove prices down

questions.question: The just transition requires that:
options: Coal power stays dominant permanently
All coal workers retire immediately
Coalfield workers and towns are retrained and included in the new energy economy rather than abandoned
Renewables are built only outside coal regions

subtopics.title: Living Off the Interest — Soil and the Sustainable Year

questions.question: The teaspoon and the bucket describe:
options: Soil forming at a teaspoon a year while one storm on bare ground withdraws decades of it
The ratio of rain to evaporation
Fertiliser doses on commercial farms
The difference between rills and gullies

questions.question: In the bank-account picture, coal and sunshine differ because:
options: Both are interest arriving forever
Coal is capital — a one-time inheritance being burned — while sun and wind are interest arriving fresh forever
Sunshine is capital and coal is interest
Neither can be counted economically

questions.question: Gabions heal a donga by:
options: Poisoning the plants that caused it
Draining the water table beneath it
Sealing it under a concrete channel
Slowing each flood with rock-filled baskets until it drops its soil and the channel silts closed

questions.question: The circle of the year connects the topics as:
options: Trade causes floods which cause aid
Soil erosion causes El Niño events
Development needs energy; coal energy warms the climate; harder droughts and storms strip the soil; lost soil starves the farming development depends on
The topics are unrelated and must be studied separately
